recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-7172 unless the work group later reopens the nutrition/medication boundary for parenteral nutrition.
issue_request: FHIR-7172 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification OO issue asking whether NutritionOrder included hyperalimentation and requiring clarification that it does not, plus text explaining what providers may populate versus dietary specialists and that profiles can address variations.
initial_application: Git commit 65afef74325d40bc76731f4fe954951ebe0e3064 (#7172, #7184) added NutritionOrder introduction text excluding parenteral (IV) nutrition and describing different provider roles and order detail levels. The active NutritionOrder source still carries those semantics.
additional_context: The seed resolution pointed to Pharmacy issue FHIR-8203 for total parenteral nutrition placement. FHIR-8203 is Published/Persuasive with Modification and current MedicationRequest source includes total parenteral nutrition. Later FHIR-15943 was Resolved - No Change after noting NutritionOrder already keeps parenteral nutrition out of scope. A 2019 Zulip implementer thread also treated TPN as outside NutritionOrder.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the active NutritionOrder scope and boundary text already satisfy the issue and no source correction is needed.

related_jiras.note: Companion Pharmacy issue placing total parenteral nutrition in MedicationPrescription/MedicationRequest rather than NutritionOrder.
Later no-change NutritionOrder modeling issue notes that the introduction already limits NutritionOrder and excludes parenteral nutrition.
Later Healthcare Product boundary work references parenteral nutrition as a medication/nutrition boundary example but does not require a FHIR-7172 source change.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking to clarify that NutritionOrder does not include hyperalimentation/parenteral nutrition and to describe provider/dietitian scope.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the seed decision that the current NutritionOrder scope must satisfy.

evidence_items.summary: Active NutritionOrder source excludes parenteral IV nutrition, describes physician/dietitian/speech therapist use, and directs parenteral nutrition requests to MedicationRequest.
evidence_items.learned: The current build already conveys the requested clarification.

evidence_items.summary: The #7172/#7184 implementation commit added NutritionOrder parenteral exclusion and provider-scope prose.
evidence_items.learned: The seed was directly applied in source history and the semantics remain present.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy companion issue requiring MedicationPrescription to include total parenteral nutrition.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms the complementary placement for parenteral nutrition outside NutritionOrder.

evidence_items.summary: In 2019, participants quoted the NutritionOrder boundary and stated that TPN is explicitly out of scope for NutritionOrder.
evidence_items.learned: Later community discussion is consistent with the current source and does not require a change.
